test_title: PYST 30: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 26th November 2021 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: An article was sold at a loss of 18%. Had that article been sold for ₹ 2,475 more, there would have been a profit of 12%. Find the selling price (in ₹) of the article.
solution:
Given:

Loss on the article = 18%

Profit after adding ₹ 2,475 to SP = 12%

Formula used:

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article be q

Original selling price = q - q × 18%

⇒q - (q × 18/100) = 0.82q

Desired selling price = q + q × 12%

⇒q + (q × 12/100) = 1.12q

According to the question,

1.12q - 0.82q = 2475

⇒ 0.3q = 2475

⇒ q = 2475/0.3

⇒ q = 8250

Now, the original SP of the article = 8250 × 0.82

⇒ ₹6765

**∴ The selling price of the article was ₹6765.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__ **

Let CP be 100%, therefore

⇒ (100 - 18)% + 2475 = (100 + 12)%

⇒ 82 % + 2475 = 112%

⇒ 112% - 82% = 2475

⇒ 30% = 2475

⇒ 1% = 2475/30 = 82.5

Then SP = 82% (At 18% loss)

⇒ SP = 82.5 × 82 = 6765

∴ The selling price of the article was ₹6765.
